label: Pruss actual-absence route: laws, nonvacuity, omission, replacement and S4 conceivability models
paraphrase: Premise-free law and finite models (structural surrogates). Law: with Euclidean access the global possibility that no concrete being is contingent implies Pruss's possibility that every actual contingent concretum is absent. Models: nonvacuity of the sibling on the theist frame and on a non-Euclidean frame (the sibling needs no Euclidean premise); one omission model for each of its five non-logical premises; replacement (one actual concretum possibly absent, Pruss's premise holding, the global premise failing because a non-actual being is contingent elsewhere) and Van Cleve's point (two actual contingents, each possibly absent, never jointly absent, on a Euclidean frame: Pruss's and the global premise both fail); and, on a reflexive transitive non-Euclidean frame, #248's unrestricted conceivability bridge holding for a conceiver of both a being's necessary existence and its absence, in two models: one with the being not actual at the reading world, one with it actual there; so law 9 of the framework controls depends on Euclidean access.
